html:
SMTO-CMP-0006 — Something you asked for hasn't been confirmed yet

GUID: 54939e1f-eca2-47ce-b7b9-dfe2ecd8f38e
Slug: completion-open-requirement
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • Part of what you asked for hasn't been confirmed by SMTO yet, so it won't call the task finished. If the AI keeps answering without confirming it, the task stops as Partial. Work done so far is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the task's latest reply and open Technical details in this panel to see which requested result is still unconfirmed. SMTO lists the exact requirement it couldn't confirm, so you know what to look at.
  2. Check that result yourself, for example whether the file, setting or service now looks the way you asked. It may already be done; SMTO just hasn't seen proof of it yet.
  3. Select Resume, or in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task ask SMTO to check (not redo) that part, then select Continue. A check gives SMTO the missing confirmation without repeating changes that already happened.
  4. Don't select Restart task while you're unsure what already happened. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so changes could happen twice.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its reply confirms the result you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with what you saw when you checked the result. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't restart the task while that is unclear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • With receipt verification enabled, completion found caller requirements that no current receipt satisfies (reason open_requirement), or repeated plain final answers left the same requirements unmet until the completion-correction bound stopped the run as partial.

What this means

  • Enabled receipt verification finds open caller requirements, or repeated plain-terminal handling cannot resolve its completion requirements within the protocol bound. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Enabled receipt verification finds open caller requirements, or repeated plain-terminal handling cannot resolve its completion requirements within the protocol bound.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact open requirement and existing receipts before deciding what observation is missing.

How to fix it

  • Inspect open_requirements (and completion_unmet_details) in the run's completion.rejected event and compare each requirement's pointer and equals value with the latest current receipt (open_requirements and validate_completion in src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py; reject_answer in native/turn_results.py). Obtain the missing observation in this run and cite it, without repeating completed mutations; the completion.receipt_verification Agent Check controls enforcement.
  • Inspect the unresolved requirement and obtain its missing observation or verification.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The required outcome is established without repeating already completed mutations.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
